slides.text:
You can declare a variable with a name that is already taken. The new variable **shadows** the old one: from that line on, the name means the new value.

The old value is not changed, it just stops being reachable by that name.

Shadowing is not `mut`. It makes a brand new variable, so it can even have another type. In this module you shadow, compare it with `mut` and see how far a shadow reaches.

Pseudo code, not Rust.
slides.code:
name = first value
name = new variable, same name
  (the first one is hidden)

exercises.title: Shadow in steps
exercises.guide: Shadow one name three times: text, then a number, then a calculation. Each step prints.

chunks.guide: The same name now holds a number. This works because it is a new variable, not an assignment.
A third shadow, built from the number.

notes.text: Reads the number 7, the latest reading so far.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.explanation: Each `let n` builds on the one before: 2, then 6, then 7. The first print runs before the last shadow.

exercises.title: Meters to kilometers
exercises.guide: Reuse one name to convert a distance from meters to kilometers, printing both stages.

chunks.guide: The distance in meters, printed with a label.
Shadow the name with the same distance in kilometers. The old meters value is hidden, not changed.

notes.text: Reads the meters value, since the new distance does not exist yet.

exercises.title: Trace the price
exercises.guide: The program must print 35. Pick the name that the last shadow reads from.

slides.text:
`mut` lets one variable change its value. A shadow replaces the variable with a new one, and the new one can have a different mutability.

A shadow also lasts only as long as the braces it was declared in. Pseudo code, not Rust.

exercises.title: Freeze after changes
exercises.guide: Change a `mut` variable, then shadow it without `mut` to lock it.

chunks.guide: A counter that is allowed to change, updated twice.
Shadow it with a plain `let`. This new `total` has the same value, but it can no longer change.

notes.text: No mut here, so this one is locked.

exercises.title: Lock the score
exercises.guide: Update a `mut` score, freeze it with a shadow, then print a summary.

chunks.guide: A score that is allowed to change, updated twice.
Shadow it without `mut`. The round is over, so the score is locked.

notes.text: No mut: later lines cannot change it.

chunks.guide: A bonus, then one summary line.
chunks.text:
let bonus = 10;
    println!("score {} + bonus {} = {}", score, bonus, score + bonus);

exercises.title: A shadow inside braces
exercises.guide: A shadow ends where its braces end, and the old one comes back.

chunks.guide: Inside a pair of braces, shadow `level` and print it. The shadow lives only in here.

notes.text: Hides the outer level until the closing brace.

chunks.guide: Outside the braces, the outer `level` is back.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: One inner block shadows, the other assigns.
exercises.explanation: `let n = 9` is a shadow that ends with its braces. `n = 5` has no `let`, so it changes the outer `n` for good.
